subject: Model fit eval & open vs proprietary parity - next steps
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos@paygrid.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit eval discussion (PayGrid)

Thanks both for the demo today — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity on runtime and cost levers. A quick recap and what we need next: 

- Priority: customer support summarization and routing (mix of short and long tickets).
- Key concerns: output accuracy on our terminology, hallucination rate on policy questions, and latency under 95th pctp SLA.
- Next asks from our side:
  1) recommended model list (open variants + Redwood baselines) for an apples-to-apples eval
  2) a suggested prompt set we can run locally / via your eval harness
  3) per-model benchmark template (metrics we want: top-line F1/accuracy on labeled set, hallucination rate, median/95p latency, token cost)

If you can send the initial list and the prompt set by EOD Tuesday (Mar 3) we’ll kick off internal runs and share a labeled slice for parity thresholds. Will loop in Elena (ops) for procurement notes.

Thanks,
Carlos
Head of ML, PayGrid
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit eval discussion (PayGrid)

Hi Carlos — great to meet yesterday. Appreciate the clear priorities. Quick response and next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we’ll deliver by Tue EOD (Mar 3):
- Recommended model matrix: 3 open candidates + Redwood-verified proprietary baseline (for cost/quality comparison).
- Prompt set (attached as prompt_set_paygrid_v2.txt) that mirrors the ticket mix you described.
- Benchmark template and scoring sheet (we’ll populate initial run on our side and share CSV).

Acceptance thresholds to test (proposed — happy to adjust):
- Parity = open model within 5% absolute of Redwood baseline on labeled accuracy/F1 on core triage set.
- Hallucination: <= 2% on policy QA set.
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 450ms for short tickets (<=200 tokens) under your expected QPS profile.

Marissa (SE) will run the initial server-side eval and attach the first pass results. If you agree to the thresholds above, we’ll prioritize the parity report and flag any quality regressions.

Next call: propose Tue Mar 4 11:00am PT to review initial numbers and align on any prompt tuning.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos@paygrid.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit eval discussion (PayGrid) — initial eval artifacts attached

Hey team — attaching the artifacts Carlos asked for and a short notes summary from the run we kicked off this morning. Attachments: prompt_set_paygrid_v2.txt, eval_results_v1.csv, benchmark_open_vs_proprietary.pdf 

Run notes (initial server-side eval):
- Models tested (initial sweep):
  * open-7b-v1 (quantized 4-bit) — fast, lower context handling on long tickets
  * open-13b-qa (8-bit) — better factuality on policy Q&A
  * open-7b-instruct (int8) — strong on brief summaries, weaker on multi-step reasoning
  * redwood-pro-1.0 (baseline proprietary) — highest accuracy, higher token cost
- Quick observations:
  * open-13b-qa is closest to parity on the policy QA slice but costlier than open-7b variants.
  * Hallucination probe (50 curated prompts): redwood-pro-1.0 = 1.4%, open-13b-qa = 2.6%, open-7b-v1 = 4.8%.
  * Latency (95p) under our test harness (batched 8): open-7b-v1 = 320ms, open-13b-qa = 510ms, redwood-pro-1.0 = 460ms.

Proposed immediate steps:
1) You run the prompt_set_paygrid_v2 locally / in your environment and share the labeled slice you mentioned (even 500 examples will help).
2) We’ll run a tuned prompt pass against open-13b-qa and open-7b-instruct to see if parity can be reached with prompt engineering + light calibration.
3) If parity is close, we’ll provide a cost/throughput recommendation and a suggested quantization profile for production.

Notes on risks: prompt sensitivity — small prompt changes moved accuracy 2-4% in our internal tests. Also some hallucination behaviour persists on policy Q&A, especially with short prompts lacking context.

Let me know if you want raw logs or the run config.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Vega <carlos@paygrid.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit eval discussion (PayGrid) — initial eval artifacts attached

Thanks Marissa — this is extremely helpful. Couple quick clarifying points before we run the local slice: 

- On parity thresholds: the 5% absolute on accuracy sounds reasonable, but for hallucination we care more about worst-case on policy questions. If open-13b-qa sits at ~2.6% on your probe, we’ll need to see whether those are high-severity hallucinations (policy-violating) vs low-impact ones. Can you add a severity tag to the hallucination cases in the CSV?
- Perf: open-13b-qa 95p at 510ms is slightly above our target. Can you share the VM/GPU profile and batch config used for that run? We need to evaluate if optimizations (int8 + kernel selection) can get us <480ms.
- Procurement question: if we choose a dedicated variant later, what delta in pricing should we expect between redwood-pro-1.0 and an open-13b-qa hosted config (estimate per 1M tokens)?

I’ll run the prompt set on our side this afternoon and share labeled results by EOD. Accepting Tue Mar 4 11:00am PT call to review tuning and severity tagging.

Carlos
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit eval discussion (PayGrid) — next steps & meeting

Thanks Carlos — appreciate the quick turnaround and for running the slice. Quick alignment before the 11:00am PT sync: 

Action items (we’ll own items 1-3, PayGrid owns 4):
1) Redwood: add severity tagging to hallucination cases in eval_results_v1.csv and re-run the hallucination probe with severity buckets (low/medium/high). (Owner: Marissa)
2) Redwood: include run config (GPU type, batch size, quantization) for each model in an appendix in the benchmark PDF. (Owner: Marissa)
3) Redwood: publish a short cost delta estimate (hosted per-1M-token) between redwood-pro-1.0 and open-13b-qa hosted config so Elena can budget. (Owner: Lauren)
4) PayGrid: share labeled 500-example slice from prompt_set_paygrid_v2.txt by EOD today. (Owner: Carlos)

Meeting: Tue Mar 4 11:00am PT — confirm (inv sent). If you prefer Wed, we can move.

One more note on acceptance: if open-13b-qa meets parity on accuracy and the high-severity hallucination rate is <=1.5% we’ll deliver a formal recommendation for an open-model pilot. Anything outside that and we’ll outline mitigation (prompt tuning, hybrid routing to redwood-pro-1.0 for policy Q&A).

Thanks — talk soon.

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
